highlights: Samsung Galaxy Smart Tag 2 Bluetooth Tracker
Compass View AR, Find Lost Mode
Enhanced battery life: SmartTag2 luggage tracker with up to 500 days of lifespan, Power Saving Mode extending it by up to 40%, ensures reliable tracking on your journeys¹
Durable and water-resistant design: With an IP67 rating, the SmartTag2 is built to withstand dust and water, making it a robust and convenient travel companion² ³ ⁴

Find it in lost mode: When Lost Mode is activated, the Galaxy smart tag's NFC (Near Field Communication) displays your registered contact information and message on the finder's smartphone, regardless of the OS⁵

Compass mode: Switch on Search Nearby to get intuitive step-by-step instructions via Compass View, or opt for Ring Your Tag to have your smart tracker audibly signal its whereabouts to help you locate it effortlessly⁶ ⁷ ⁸

Give it a way back to you. When Lost Mode is activated, the Galaxy tracker device’s NFC (Near Field Communication) displays your registered contact information and message on the finder's smartphone, regardless of the OS.⁵

¹Battery life, which is based on results from internal lab tests conducted by Samsung for typical usage pattern scenarios, is a simulated value of the total battery consumption measured by analyzing normal usage patterns and the current required for each function with the duration of time of each function. Tested with results from a pre-release version of the device using inbox CR2032 battery. Actual battery life may vary depending on different usage patterns, device model, or the battery manufacturer.

²Galaxy SmartTag2 is rated as IP67. Based on lab test conditions for submersion in up to 1 meter of freshwater for up to 30 minutes. Not advised for beach, pool use or soapy water. Water and dust resistance of device is not permanent and may diminish over time.

³IoT devices need to be registered within the SmartThings app for features to properly function. SmartTag2 must be connected to the user’s mobile device. Devices compatible with the SmartThings app can be checked on the SmartThings website.
⁴When on Power Saving Mode, some of the features, such as Search Nearby, IoT control and others, may become inaccessible with the exception of basic finding function which uses Bluetooth.

⁵Contact information and message must be registered beforehand on the SmartThings app to have it shown on the finder's device on Lost Mode. The finder's device must support NFC reading, be connected to the internet and enabled to display the pre-registered contact information upon tagging. Feature availability may vary depending on the device compatibility.
